question.worked_solution:
First we apply the quotient rule, subtracting exponents in the fraction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{u}^{5}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{{u}^{4}} & = \\ {u}^{5}\cdot {u}^{2-4} & = \\ {u}^{5}\cdot {u}^{-2} & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Then we apply the product rule, adding exponents in the product:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{u}^{5}\cdot {u}^{-2} & = \\ {u}^{5+(-2)} & = \\ {u}^{5-2} & = \\ {u}^{3} & \end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{u}^{5}\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{{u}^{4}}={u}^{3}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
